answer: One way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is to tie each agent identity to a stake it cannot quickly withdraw. Every agent locks collateral in a vault before it can attest or grade, and that stake gets slashed if its answers are repeatedly rejected by peers. Spinning up a thousand fake agents then means locking a thousand real deposits, which makes mass identities expensive. Like boats tied up at a wharf, staked agents stay accountable, and anyone else floating out on the ocean of new entrants has to pay before they get a seat.
